newsitem.title: USA: Cincinnati Bengals football to play in new stadium.
newsitem.headline: Cincinnati Bengals football to play in new stadium.

text.p: Cincinnati Bengals owner Mike Brown signed a lease Thursday to run until 2026 to play in a new 66,900-seat football stadium to be named after the NFL team's founder, his father Paul Brown.
The planned $270 million Paul Brown Stadium will be built adjacent to Cinergy Field, the riverfront arena where the Bengals will continue to play until the new stadium is ready in 2000.
"This binds the Bengals to Cincinnati -- where we always wanted to be -- for generations to come," said Brown, president and general manager.
Naming the stadium after the late Paul Brown -- the founder, owner and longtime coach of the Bengals -- had been a closely guarded secret revealed for the first time at Thursday's ceremony.
The Bengals flirted with Baltimore as a possible home for the franchise, which spurred Hamilton County voters in March 1996 to pass a 0.5 percent increase in the local sales tax.
The tax was designed to finance construction of two new stadiums, one for the Bengals and one for the Cincinnati Reds baseball team. Currently, the two teams share Cinergy Field.
Plans for the new baseball stadium have proceeded much more slowly with no decision yet on where it will be located.

Brown and the Hamilton County commissioners, the county's three-man governing body, unveiled a model of the stadium, which he described as a "cutting-edge" structure showing the way for a new generation of stadium design.
"This stadium has more than 70 percent of its seats along the sidelines," Brown said. "That's unique among stadiums."
It also will have a roof overhanging all the seats to protect fans from the elements.

The agreement, reached after 14 months of negotiations, called for the Bengals to contribute more than $44 million to the stadium project, but pay no rental for the last 16 years of the lease. The first nine nine years will cost them $11.7 million in rent.
